title: Served-acceptance report
description: One arm of a served-acceptance measurement: one drafter (or none) on one runtime, one prompt corpus, one budget. bench/REPORTS.md is the specification; this schema covers the per-field rules. The cross-field rules (token accounting, round chronology, unique prompts, a complete arm) are in REPORTS.md and are enforced by bench/analysis/validate_report.py and by the analyser. Counts must be JSON integer literals: the analyser refuses 4.0 and true where it expects a count, so 'integer' here means an integer literal, not any integral number. The analyser also enforces these per-field rules itself: integer max_new and cap of at least 1, temperature 0, a string category, a boolean thinking, integer response_ids and a positive decode_seconds.

drafter.description: Label of the drafter. null only for an arm without a drafter (the target's own autoregressive path). Not read by the analyser.

complete.description: false until every prompt's record has been written. Writers save the partial report as they go; the analyser refuses an arm that is not complete.

requests.description: One record per prompt, in corpus order. Paired arms must list the same prompts in the same order.

mode.description: Adapter-specific, optional (dflash-mlx-bonsai2). 'speculative' for a drafter arm, 'target_only' for the target's autoregressive path.

arm.description: Adapter-specific, optional (dflash-mlx-bonsai2). Per-arm details that must not be in settings because they legitimately differ between paired arms: paths, file hashes, load time. Not read by the analyser.

summary.description: Adapter-specific, optional (dflash-mlx-bonsai2, written with complete=true). Pooled figures for a reader; the analyser recomputes everything from requests and does not read this.

settings.description: Everything two paired arms must share. The analyser compares the whole object for equality and refuses the pair on any difference, so per-arm details (paths, hashes, timings) belong elsewhere. Writers add their own keys; only max_new, cap and temperature are required.

max_new.description: The requested token budget, counting the prefill's own token.

cap.description: The most drafts one block can carry. One block is cap + 1 tokens: the drafts plus the target's own token from the same verify pass.

temperature.description: Both contracts assume greedy decoding. The analyser refuses a report without this key or with any other value (0.0 is the same number; false is not); both writers record 0.0.

target.description: Label of the target model, with its revision where known.

split.description: The corpus split the prompts were taken from.

kv_bits.description: KV cache precision in bits, or null for an unquantized cache.

bits.description: mlx-dspark: the drafter's served precision in bits; 0 is bf16.

corpus_sha256.description: sha256 of the corpus file, lowercase hex.

prompt_sha256.description: sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of Python's json.dumps(prompt_ids) with default separators, i.e. '[1, 2, 3]', as lowercase hex. Must be unique within a report.

category.description: The prompt's stratum for the bootstrap and the breakdown; 'unknown' when the corpus row has none.

thinking.description: Whether the templated prompt enables thinking. A stratum, like category.

tokens.description: Emitted tokens, counting the prefill's own token. Equals len(response_ids).

rounds.description: Speculative rounds (verify passes that emitted at least one token). The prefill's token belongs to no round.

round_lengths.description: Optional; required by the equivalence contract. Tokens each round committed: the drafts it accepted plus the target's own token. Length equals rounds.

finish.description: 'length' when the run stopped on the budget, 'stop' when it stopped on a stop token.

response_ids.description: The emitted token ids, in order, starting with the prefill's own token and ending at the first stop token if there is one.

decode_seconds.description: Wall time after prefill. Carried for throughput readers; no contract compares it.

runtime.description: Adapter-specific, optional (dflash-mlx-bonsai2). The runtime loop's own per-pass record, unmapped, so its native bookkeeping can be recomputed. Not read by the analyser.
